summary: check no longer stops when a course workspace's closure days haven't been entered. --closures is passed only when somebody has said what the days are: a list from the workspace, an empty list for a course that closes on no days, or the flag the caller gave outside Canvas Builder. When nobody has said, the flag is left off altogether, cb-checks reports its closure-day rule as not checked and checks the rest of the dates, and check exits 0. MsgNoClosureDays is gone, along with the exit-10 refusal it carried; the recipes and SKILL.md now tell the agent to pass the not-checked entry on instead of running the other three checks by name.
reason:
JR-59. The check-command patch refused `check dates` and `check all` with MsgNoClosureDays and exit 10 whenever the workspace listed no closure days. The list is the instructor's to enter and the agent cannot supply it, so an agent that hits this learns to stop running `check all` -- the one command it reaches for first -- over one rule of one check. Closure days drive exactly one rule in cb-checks (due-on-closure); date-outside-course, date-order and date-in-text need none of them. SPEC §7 already says a check never goes silent and still exits 0, so canvas-builder-v2 commit 2f1ebda taught cb-checks to tell `closures: null` (nobody has said) from `closures: []` (closes on no days) and to report the first as one not-checked entry about the course. This patch is the CLI side of that: the only way to say "nobody has said" on a command line is to leave the flag off.

It also makes `check dates --course N` outside Canvas Builder honest. It passed an empty --closures when the caller gave none, so the closure-day rule ran against an empty list and was reported as passed.

The check-command patch's known_limitations describes the old refusal and is superseded here.

A deliberate deviation from the issue, which asked for `check all` to fan out while standalone `check dates` kept exiting 10. Exit 10 prints no report, so an agent that asked for the date check by name would be told nothing at all about the three rules that did run, and 10 means a config fault, which an unentered list isn't. One report that says which rule couldn't be applied is more use than a refusal, and it is what SPEC §7 asks for. CodeRabbit raised the same point twice against the issue text; both were skipped for this reason.
known_limitations:
The two halves agree by contract, not by type: the CLI leaves a flag off and cb-checks reads its absence as null. TestCheckRealHelperWithoutClosureDays runs the real cb-checks and asserts the not-checked entry comes back, but it skips without CANVAS_BUILDER_V2 and node, so an ordinary `go test ./...` proves only the argv.

runChecks takes days as a *string. A nil pointer and a pointer to "" are two different answers one character apart, which is easy to get wrong in a later edit; the tests pin both.

In Canvas Builder, `--closures` with nothing after it is still accepted and ignored, as before. Only a non-empty value is refused with MsgClosuresFromWorkspace.

MsgNoClosureDays is removed rather than kept unused. Nothing else referred to it, and Canvas Builder has never shown it to anyone: it only ever reached an agent.
validated_outcome:
gofmt clean on every file touched. go build ./... and go vet ./... clean. go test ./... passing on darwin/arm64. CANVAS_BUILDER_V2=/Users/johnnyrobot/code/canvas-builder-v2 go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestCheckRealHelper passing against canvas-builder-v2 at 2f1ebda on node v22, both the placeholders case and the new closure-days one.

TestCheckNeedsClosureDays is now TestCheckClosureDays, covering the three answers a workspace can give. Nothing said with `check dates`, with `check a11y` and with `check all` each exit 0 and run with no --closures in the argv; an empty list runs with `--closures ""`. TestCheckOutsideCanvasBuilder gains "no closure days given": `check dates --course 7` with no flag exits 0 and runs with no --closures. TestCheckRealHelperWithoutClosureDays runs the real cb-checks with OmitClosureDays and asserts one issue, rule not-checked, item.type "course", its message naming the closure days.
